practiceNotes: Recall practice maintains concepts, representations, assumptions and method selection. Assess proofs, programs, experiments and extended interpretations separately on unseen tasks.

Require reproducible records, uncertainty analysis, alternative explanations and individual defenses within team projects. Distinguish operating supplied software, implementing its algorithm and proving its guarantees.
Laboratory competence requires appropriate facilities and supervised hands-on assessment; simulated or archived data alone do not certify practical competence.
Human, animal, genomic and field investigations require applicable consent, welfare, ethics, collection and data-governance approvals. Biological engineering uses approved contained low-risk systems.
Security exercises require owned or explicitly authorized isolated systems. Cryptographic teaching implementations are not production security products.
Hazardous chemicals, radiation, lasers, high voltage, pressure and moving machinery require facility-specific training and authorization.

Computational projects may use documented numerical libraries where the contract says to use a tool; implementation assessments must expose the stated algorithm rather than hide it behind a library call.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Foundations of Life
decks.description: Explain common organization and diversity of life.

includes: Cells, organisms, energy, heredity, evolution, ecosystems and biological evidence.

practice: Construct linked cell, inheritance and ecosystem explanations and revise them when supplied contradictory evidence.

outcomes.description: Distinguish observation, hypothesis and mechanism; identify controls and alternative explanations in biological investigations.
Explain genes, reproduction, variation and selection; read elementary pedigrees, evolutionary trees and food webs.
Compare cellular and organismal organization; explain membranes, biological molecules, energy transformations and homeostasis with diagrams.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations
decks.description: Turn explicit procedures into reliable programs.

includes: Structured programming, collections, files, modules, debugging and tests; notation taught from scratch.

practice: Implement a file-processing application with malformed-input tests and a reproducible execution script.

outcomes.description: Represent records with arrays, lists and maps; parse files, validate inputs and define module interfaces.
Write and trace variables, Boolean expressions, branches, loops, functions, recursion and simple classes.
Debug using traces and assertions; design boundary tests and explain termination and elementary operation counts.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantitative Foundations
decks.description: Develop numerical, symbolic and spatial literacy.

includes: Arithmetic, units, algebra, elementary functions, Euclidean geometry, trigonometry and vectors.

practice: Model a measured object's geometry and scaling, reconciling numerical, graphical and symbolic answers.

outcomes.description: Translate formulas, tables and graphs; manipulate polynomial, exponential and logarithmic functions, inverses and elementary equations.
Calculate lengths, areas and volumes; use Cartesian coordinates, radians, trigonometry, and two- or three-dimensional vectors and dot products.
Calculate fractions, powers, scientific notation, ratios and unit conversions; solve linear and quadratic equations and check scale.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Matter and Chemical Quantities
decks.description: Represent matter and calculate chemical transformations.

includes: Atomic composition, bonding, formulas, stoichiometry, gases, solutions and reaction notation.

practice: Infer a simple mixture's composition from masses and reactions, checking material and charge balances.

outcomes.description: Convert mass, moles, particle counts and concentrations; balance equations and calculate limiting reagents, yields and ideal-gas quantities.
Represent precipitation, dissolution, acid-base and redox reactions with conserved atoms and charge.
Use isotopes, electron configurations, Lewis structures, resonance and molecular geometry to explain periodicity, polarity and intermolecular forces.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Digital Logic and Architecture
decks.description: Connect software execution to digital hardware.

includes: Binary encodings, Boolean circuits, state machines, instruction sets, datapaths and memory hierarchy.

practice: Build an instruction-set emulator and cache experiment and reconcile counts with measured timing.

outcomes.description: Calculate integer and floating-point encodings and construct combinational and clocked circuits from truth tables and state diagrams.
Trace assembly calls, registers, addresses and stacks; implement a simple processor datapath and control simulator.
Analyze caches, virtual addresses, pipelines and hazards and calculate latency and throughput under explicit assumptions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus

includes: Limits, derivatives, integrals, series and one-variable approximation.

practice: Analyze variable-rate accumulation and bound the error of a local polynomial approximation.

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and derivatives; apply chain and implicit differentiation, optimization and local linearization.
Evaluate definite and improper integrals using substitution and integration by parts; explain the fundamental theorem and accumulation models.
Test series convergence and construct Taylor expansions with stated intervals and error bounds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Data and Empirical Inference
decks.description: Make defensible elementary empirical inferences.

includes: Descriptive statistics, elementary probability, resampling, tests, intervals and study design.

practice: Analyze imperfect data using an explicitly taught spreadsheet resampling procedure and defend the sampling unit and uncertainty claims.

outcomes.description: Summarize numerical and categorical data; calculate variation, correlation and least-squares lines and distinguish association from causation.
Design sampling and randomized comparisons; identify confounding, pseudoreplication, missingness, multiplicity and misleading uncertainty.
Use finite probability, binomial and normal models, bootstrap intervals, permutation tests, t tests and contingency tables with explicit assumptions.

practice: Write proofs of graph invariants and counting identities and construct counterexamples to false generalizations.

outcomes.description: Count using bijections, combinations and inclusion-exclusion; solve elementary recurrences and finite counting-probability problems.
Translate quantified statements and construct direct, contradiction, contrapositive and induction proofs; diagnose invalid arguments.
Manipulate sets, functions, equivalence relations, orders and graphs; prove elementary connectivity, tree and congruence properties.

practice: Analyze an overdetermined measurement system through elimination, projection and singular values, including sensitivity.

Calculate complex eigenvalues, diagonalizations, orthogonal or unitary bases and singular-value decompositions; interpret conditioning and quadratic forms.
Solve linear systems by elimination; calculate rank, null spaces and determinants and interpret inconsistency or nonuniqueness.

Implement heaps, hash tables, balanced trees and graph representations; select structures by operations and memory cost.
