Describe unit cells, lattice energetics and defects and predict simple preparation and stability from equilibrium and redox evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Laboratory Practice
decks.description: Perform controlled chemical measurements and separations.

includes: Standards, wet quantitative methods, separations, uncertainty, records and hazard control.

practice: Separate and quantify a benign mixture under supervision with mass balance, uncertainty and a written risk assessment.

outcomes.description: Prepare standards and perform volumetry, gravimetry and calorimetry with blanks, calibration, replicates and an uncertainty budget.
Select containment, substitutions, protective measures and waste handling from hazard and exposure evidence and justify tradeoffs.
Perform extraction, recrystallization, distillation and thin-layer chromatography; explain recovery, partitioning, volatility and purity limits.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure and Reactivity
decks.description: Explain organic structures and transformations.

includes: Organic spatial representations, stereochemistry, functional-group mechanisms and empirical IR and NMR interpretation.

practice: Identify unknown isomers and defend mechanism-supported short synthetic sequences against alternative products.

outcomes.description: Infer small-molecule structures from formula, unsaturation, taught IR bands and proton or carbon NMR shifts, integration and coupling rules.
Draw substitution, elimination, addition, aromatic and carbonyl mechanisms and predict chemo-, regio- and stereoselectivity.
Translate skeletal, wedge-dash, Newman and chair representations; assign stereochemistry and compare conformational, resonance and acid-base effects.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Physical Chemistry
decks.description: Derive quantitative models of chemical change.

includes: Chemical potentials, activities, phase and electrochemical equilibria, mechanism kinetics and simple diffusion.

practice: Compare reaction mechanisms and construct a nonideal equilibrium model with parameter and approximation uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Derive chemical equilibrium from potentials and calculate nonideal activities, phase diagrams, colligative effects and electrochemical potentials.
Derive mechanism ODEs, steady-state and pre-equilibrium limits, Arrhenius relations and one-dimensional steady diffusion; compare parameters by explicit grid residual fitting and sensitivity checks.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Search, Reasoning and Planning
decks.description: Build symbolic agents from explicit representations.

includes: State-space search, constraints, symbolic reasoning, planning and adversarial games.

practice: Build a planning or game agent, prove a bounded guarantee and investigate representation-dependent failures.

outcomes.description: Implement classical planning and minimax pruning and compare representation and heuristic failures.
Represent propositional and restricted first-order knowledge and implement unification and resolution or rule inference with soundness arguments.
Implement uniform-cost, A-star and constraint search and prove completeness and optimality conditions.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Database Systems
decks.description: Preserve and query persistent information.

includes: Relational modeling, SQL, normalization, query planning, indexing and transaction semantics.

practice: Build a transactional application, inspect query plans and reproduce isolation anomalies.

outcomes.description: Construct schemas, keys and constraints and derive normalization from functional dependencies.
Write relational-algebra and SQL queries and analyze joins, B-tree indexes and cost-based plans with cardinality estimates.
Analyze serializability, isolation anomalies and logging and compare relational and document models for stated workloads.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Graphics and Visualization
decks.description: Construct images and faithful visual explanations.

includes: Spatial transforms, projection, rasterization, visibility, color, image filtering and visualization.

practice: Build a rasterizer and scientific visualization and validate geometry and encoding choices.

outcomes.description: Implement homogeneous-coordinate transforms, perspective cameras, clipping, barycentric rasterization and depth-buffer visibility for polygonal scenes.
Implement discrete image filtering and color conversion and design visual encodings that account for scale, uncertainty, distortion and accessibility.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Languages and Compilers
decks.description: Implement a language and its execution model.

includes: Evaluation semantics, lexing, parsing, typing, translation, closures, memory management and optimization.

practice: Build a typed interpreter and small compiler with scope, memory and translation-preservation tests.

outcomes.description: Implement stack frames and closures and explain tracing collection and data-flow optimization with preservation tests.
Specify scope, closures, mutation, evaluation order and type rules and compare programming paradigms through interpreters.
Construct finite-state lexers and grammar-based parsers, type-check syntax trees and lower them through intermediate representations to machine code.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Software Engineering
decks.description: Deliver maintainable software with justified assurance.

includes: Requirements, modular architecture, testing, elementary verification, collaboration and professional judgment.

practice: Build a team application with individually defended architecture, a verified core routine and an evidence-based release decision.

outcomes.description: Construct unit, integration and property tests; prove loop contracts and check finite-state safety by exhaustive exploration.
Use version control, review and continuous integration and justify accessibility, privacy, licensing and reliability decisions.
Translate requirements into interfaces and modular architectures and compare functional and object-oriented designs.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Operating Systems
decks.description: Implement and diagnose operating-system mechanisms.

includes: Low-level programming, processes, memory, synchronization, files and crash recovery.

practice: Build a concurrent persistent service with injected crashes and traced resource behavior.

outcomes.description: Implement synchronized threaded programs and diagnose races, deadlock and ordering failures through interleavings.
Use pointers, explicit memory management and system calls; implement scheduling, allocation and page-replacement simulations.
Explain files, block storage, caching and journaling; implement a persistent store and test interrupted-write recovery.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Theory of Computation
decks.description: Establish computational possibilities and limits.

includes: Automata, grammars, computability, reductions and time and space complexity.

practice: Write complete automata and reduction proofs and executable small-machine examples.

outcomes.description: Define time and space classes, P, NP and completeness and construct polynomial reductions with explicit resource accounting.
Represent computation by Turing machines and prove undecidability and recognizability claims using diagonalization and reductions.
Construct finite and pushdown automata and regular or context-free grammars and prove language membership and nonmembership.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Prove and calculate complex-variable results.

includes: Holomorphic functions, complex contours, residues, conformal maps and analytic continuation.

practice: Develop contour proofs and solve a planar mapping problem, identifying invalid deformations.

outcomes.description: Verify complex differentiability and Cauchy-Riemann conditions and prove power-series consequences of analyticity.
Evaluate real and inverse-transform integrals by contours and construct conformal maps with explicit branch choices.
Prove and apply Cauchy theorems, Laurent expansions and residue formulas with contour and singularity conditions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry
decks.description: Calculate coordinate-independent geometric quantities.

includes: Curves, surfaces, charts, tangent spaces, metrics, tensors and differential forms.

practice: Compute curved-surface quantities in two charts and prove their transformation rules.

outcomes.description: Calculate arc length, curvature, torsion, fundamental forms and Gaussian curvature and distinguish intrinsic and embedding-dependent quantities.
Use charts, tangent and cotangent bases, tensor transformations, pullbacks and differential forms to calculate invariant lengths and integrals.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra
decks.description: Use advanced algebraic correspondences.

includes: Galois theory, modules, tensor products, representations, commutative algebra and affine varieties.

practice: Complete a Galois or representation calculation and an affine-variety analysis with proofs.

outcomes.description: Prove the finite Galois correspondence and calculate groups, intermediate fields and solvability for concrete polynomials.
Use localization, Noetherian rings and ideal-variety correspondence to analyze affine examples, dimension and singularities.
Analyze modules over principal ideal domains, tensor products and finite-group representations and derive structure and character decompositions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure Theory
decks.description: Develop rigorous integration and convergence tools.

includes: Measures, measurable functions, Lebesgue integration, product measures and differentiation of measures.

practice: Write measure-construction and convergence proofs and demonstrate failure when hypotheses are removed.

outcomes.description: Prove and apply monotone and dominated convergence, product integration and Radon-Nikodym results with precise hypotheses.
Construct measures through outer measures and prove measurability and approximation results for sets and functions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Analysis
decks.description: Implement reliable numerical approximations.

includes: Floating-point error, numerical solvers, interpolation, quadrature and ODE integration.

practice: Build a tested numerical library and separate model, discretization, conditioning and roundoff errors.

outcomes.description: Implement polynomial and spline interpolation and quadrature and derive elementary error estimates.
Implement Euler, Runge-Kutta and implicit ODE steps and analyze consistency, stability and refinement convergence.
Implement pivoted elimination, iterative linear methods and bracketed or Newton root finding and analyze conditioning and convergence.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization
decks.description: Formulate optimization problems and justify algorithms.

includes: Convexity, constrained optimization, linear programming, duality and gradient methods.

practice: Solve constrained estimation and allocation problems and compare iterations with optimality certificates.

outcomes.description: Implement gradient, Newton and projected methods with line search; prove elementary convergence bounds and diagnose scaling and constraint failures.
Establish convexity and derive optimality, multiplier and KKT conditions; formulate linear programs and interpret dual certificates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations
decks.description: Formulate and solve spatial models analytically.

includes: Linear transport, wave, heat and elliptic PDEs, boundary conditions, Fourier transforms and Green functions.

practice: Solve a two-dimensional boundary problem and a wave or diffusion initial-value problem and check their boundary and limiting behavior.

outcomes.description: Derive conservation-based PDEs and classify elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic models with appropriate initial and boundary conditions.
Solve one- to three-dimensional standard problems using characteristics, separation, explicitly developed Fourier transforms and Green functions; establish elementary uniqueness and energy estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability
decks.description: Calculate uncertainty from explicit probability models.

includes: Discrete and continuous distributions, joint densities, conditioning, finite Markov chains and elementary limit laws.

practice: Analyze a finite reliability chain and a continuous random-vector model, comparing exact probabilities with approximations.

outcomes.description: Calculate conditional probabilities, Bayes updates and covariance; analyze finite Markov-chain transitions and stationary distributions.
Derive elementary probability bounds and moment identities and apply laws of large numbers and central-limit approximations with checked conditions.
Construct distributions and joint densities; calculate moments, marginal distributions and transformed densities using Jacobians.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Point-Set Topology
decks.description: Reason about general spaces and continuity.

includes: Topological spaces, products, quotients, continuity, compactness, connectedness and separation.

practice: Analyze quotient spaces and prove or refute proposed homeomorphisms using topological properties.

outcomes.description: Prove compactness and connectedness results and construct counterexamples distinguishing local, sequential and global properties.
Construct metric, product and quotient topologies and prove continuity and separation properties using open sets.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electromagnetic Field Theory
decks.description: Predict electromagnetic fields in space and matter.

includes: Static fields, boundary methods, Maxwell equations, material response, propagation and radiation.

practice: Solve a boundary problem by two methods and infer a bounded source distribution from field observations.

outcomes.description: Derive integral and differential Maxwell equations, material boundary conditions, energy flow and plane-wave propagation.
Calculate simple waveguide modes, polarization and dipole radiation and relate source geometry to measured angular patterns.
Solve static-field problems using potentials, images, multipoles and explicitly developed Cartesian or spherical separation of variables.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics
decks.description: Build calibrated measurement chains.

includes: Analog electronics, noise, sampling, spectral analysis, acquisition and experimental design.

practice: Build a sensor-amplifier-acquisition chain and investigate a weak signal with noise and systematic-error analyses.

outcomes.description: Design model-discriminating experiments and justify instrument choice, controls, safety and treatment of anomalies.
Acquire time series and use explicitly taught discrete Fourier and documented FFT procedures; estimate parameters, calibration uncertainty and systematic bias.
Design amplifiers and filters using taught operational-amplifier models and calculate transfer functions, noise budgets, sampling limits and lock-in response.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Newtonian Mechanics
decks.description: Solve calculus-based mechanical models before analytical mechanics.

includes: Variable-force motion, drag, oscillation, torque, angular momentum and rigid rotation.

practice: Compare analytic drag or oscillator solutions with measurements and derive a rolling body's motion.

outcomes.description: Formulate and solve one- and two-dimensional variable-force and drag equations; derive work and impulse integrals and forced-oscillation responses.
Define cross products and torque in Cartesian components; calculate moments of inertia by one-variable integration and solve fixed-axis rotation and rolling constraints.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Observational Astronomy
decks.description: Acquire and interpret astronomical evidence accessibly.

includes: Sky coordinates, telescopes, image calibration, photometry, spectroscopy and elementary remote inference.

practice: Reduce telescope or archive observations to a calibrated light curve and defend a remote inference.

outcomes.description: Infer bounded distances, temperatures, velocities and periodic signals using taught parallax, flux, spectral and Doppler models and evaluate extinction and selection bias.
Transform elementary sky coordinates and calibrate images with bias, dark and flat corrections; calculate angular resolution, aperture photometry and magnitude uncertainties.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Calculate quantum states and measurable consequences.

includes: Quantum probability and measurement, spatial Schrödinger equations, spin, angular momentum and approximations.

practice: Solve a spatial bound-state problem and estimate a perturbed energy and transition strength.

outcomes.description: Separate three-dimensional central-potential equations in spherical coordinates and calculate hydrogenic, spin and elementary coupled-angular-momentum states.
Apply nondegenerate perturbation and variational methods, identical-particle symmetry and dipole-transition rules with explicit validity checks.
Solve and normalize one-dimensional well, barrier and oscillator states and calculate tunneling, currents and wave-packet evolution.
Define Born probabilities, densities, expectations and variances; use complex state vectors, Hermitian operators and unitary evolution to calculate measurements.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Animal Behavior
decks.description: Investigate behavior independently of advanced neural mechanisms.

includes: Ethograms, behavioral sampling, learning, communication, social behavior and functional explanations.

practice: Code approved behavioral observations and test competing social or foraging explanations with blinded scoring.

outcomes.description: Compare proximate, developmental and evolutionary explanations of foraging, communication, mating and cooperation using explicit payoff and inclusive-fitness examples.
Construct ethograms and use focal, scan and event sampling; assess observer agreement and distinguish learning from habituation and performance changes.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biochemistry and Metabolism
decks.description: Connect molecular chemistry with biological function.

includes: Biomolecular structure, binding, enzymes, bioenergetics and central metabolism.

practice: Analyze enzyme and isotope-tracing data with carbon, electron and energy balances.

outcomes.description: Apply taught binding and Michaelis-Menten models; estimate parameters by explicit grid residual minimization and distinguish inhibition models and limitations.
Trace atoms, electrons and energy through respiration, photosynthesis and biosynthesis and interpret isotope and metabolite perturbations.
Read biomolecular sequences and three-dimensional structures and relate folding, domains and noncovalent binding to function.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Biology
decks.description: Calculate and infer evolutionary change.

includes: Selection, drift, phylogenetic inference, adaptation, speciation and historical evolution.

practice: Compare demographic and selective explanations of allele data and defend competing phylogenies.

outcomes.description: Evaluate adaptation, sexual selection, speciation and macroevolution through comparative, fossil and experimental evidence.
Construct small parsimony and distance trees and compute likelihood under a taught independent-site substitution model, assessing homoplasy and uncertainty.
Calculate Hardy-Weinberg expectations and selection, mutation and migration recurrences and compare drift using finite-population binomial sampling.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Analytical Chemistry
decks.description: Select and validate chemical measurements.

includes: Calibration, spectroscopy, chromatography, mass spectrometry, electroanalysis and identification.

practice: Validate an unknown-mixture analysis using two complementary methods and matrix controls.

outcomes.description: Infer identities and mixture composition from complementary measurements and distinguish sensitivity, selectivity, resolution and uncertainty.
Explain and operate bounded UV-visible, IR, NMR, mass-spectrometric, chromatographic and potentiometric methods using taught response and separation models.
Construct external, internal-standard and standard-addition calibrations and estimate recovery, detection limits and matrix effects.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Materials and Polymer Chemistry
decks.description: Relate chemical structure and processing to function.

includes: Polymerization, polymer architecture, defects, processing, phase behavior and material properties.

practice: Compare materials using structural, thermal and mechanical data and defend a processing-property hypothesis.

outcomes.description: Select processing and characterization for a material specification and justify durability, recyclability and life-cycle tradeoffs.
Relate bonding, defects, morphology and phase diagrams to thermal, mechanical, electronic and interfacial material properties.
Compare step-growth, chain-growth and network polymerization and calculate conversion and molecular-weight distributions in taught ideal models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Connect quantum molecular models to structure and spectra.

includes: Molecular orbitals, electronic approximations, molecular spectra and point-group symmetry.

practice: Solve a small molecular-orbital model and jointly interpret rotational, vibrational and electronic spectra.

outcomes.description: Derive small-basis variational molecular-orbital equations and distinguish Born-Oppenheimer, Hartree-Fock and density-functional approximations.
Calculate rotor, oscillator, anharmonic and elementary electronic spectra and infer bond lengths, force constants and transition intensities.
Construct symmetry operations, assign point groups and use character tables to derive orbital combinations and vibrational selection rules.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Graduate Algorithms and Complexity
decks.description: Prove advanced algorithmic guarantees and limitations.

includes: Randomized algorithms, concentration, approximation, relaxations and advanced complexity.

practice: Implement an advanced algorithm, prove its guarantee and construct adversarial instances exposing its limits.

outcomes.description: Construct greedy, primal-dual and relaxation-rounding approximations and prove ratios and integrality-gap bounds.
Prove selected hierarchy and space results and analyze randomized and parameterized classes with explicit reduction assumptions.
Design randomized hashing, sampling and graph algorithms and derive expectation and high-probability guarantees using developed concentration bounds.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Cryptographic Foundations
decks.description: Prove cryptographic claims without requiring system administration first.

includes: Security games, reductions, pseudorandomness, authenticated encryption, signatures and zero knowledge.

practice: Write a full game-based proof and test a toy construction, explicitly contrasting guarantees with randomness and implementation failures.

outcomes.description: Construct and analyze pseudorandom-function, authenticated-encryption and modular public-key signature schemes with explicit key, randomness and correctness requirements.
Define cryptographic interfaces, adversarial games, negligible advantage and computational assumptions and prove hybrid and reduction arguments.
Analyze a bounded identification or zero-knowledge protocol through completeness, soundness and simulation and distinguish model security from leakage.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Geometric Computer Vision
decks.description: Recover spatial structure without neural-learning prerequisites.

includes: Camera calibration, correspondence, triangulation, image restoration and inverse geometric uncertainty.

practice: Recover a scene from calibrated images and test failure under poor geometry, noise and mismatches.

outcomes.description: Implement camera calibration, epipolar constraints, feature correspondence and triangulation and identify projective and metric ambiguities.
Implement robust fitting and regularized image-restoration or reprojection objectives and evaluate residuals, degeneracy and uncertainty.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Information Theory and Coding
decks.description: Quantify communication limits and construct codes.

includes: Entropy, source coding, capacity, typical sequences and elementary error-correcting codes.

practice: Implement a compression and transmission chain and compare finite-length performance with theoretical bounds.

outcomes.description: Derive binary and Gaussian channel capacities and bounded typical-sequence coding arguments with explicit asymptotic assumptions.
Construct and decode linear codes with parity-check matrices over explicitly taught binary-field arithmetic and compare rate and correction guarantees.
Calculate entropy, relative entropy and mutual information, derive source-coding bounds and implement prefix and arithmetic coding.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks
decks.description: Construct communicating systems and diagnose failures.

includes: Layered networking, routing, reliable transport, congestion, sockets, RPC and partial failure.

practice: Build a service and transport simulator with controlled delay and loss injection.

outcomes.description: Use RPC, logical clocks and elementary replication and distinguish duplicate execution and partial failure from local concurrency.
Calculate addressing, forwarding and routing and interpret framing, naming and application protocols in packet traces.
Implement socket applications and simulated reliable transport and analyze loss, retransmission, flow control and congestion.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Parallel and High-Performance Computing
decks.description: Engineer efficient and correct parallel computation.

includes: Shared-memory and message-passing parallelism, GPU programming, locality, scaling and numerical reproducibility.

practice: Parallelize a solver in two execution models and report correctness, reproducibility and measured scalability.

outcomes.description: Analyze SIMD, caches, bandwidth and communication and derive speedup and roofline predictions.
Implement shared-memory, rank-based message-passing and GPU kernels with explicit synchronization, communication and partitioning semantics.
Profile parallel solvers and diagnose races, reduction-order error, imbalance and scaling limits through reproducible benchmarks.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Rendering and Light Transport
decks.description: Implement physically based image synthesis.

includes: Radiometry, reflection, light transport, ray tracing and Monte Carlo rendering.

practice: Compare deterministic and Monte Carlo rendering against analytic scenes with error-versus-sample studies.

outcomes.description: Implement ray intersections and importance-sampled path tracing, deriving unbiased estimators and diagnosing variance, aliasing and numerical artifacts.
Define radiance, solid angle and reflection distributions and derive direct-light and rendering integrals with energy-conservation checks.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Semantics and Formal Verification
decks.description: Prove language and program correctness.

includes: Operational and denotational semantics, type soundness, domain fixed points and stateful or concurrent verification.

practice: Formalize a small language, prove type safety and verify a concurrent component with explicit proof obligations.

outcomes.description: Define operational and denotational models, develop ordered-domain fixed points and prove bounded equivalence and adequacy properties.
Prove progress and preservation using substitution and induction and analyze explicit polymorphism, effect or subtyping rules.
Verify stateful and concurrent programs using Hoare, separation and temporal reasoning and implement finite-state model checking with abstraction-soundness arguments.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Advanced Number Theory
decks.description: Use algebraic and analytic arithmetic methods.

includes: Algebraic integers, ideals, ramification, arithmetic functions, Dirichlet series and analytic estimates.

practice: Compute an ideal-class example and prove an analytic counting estimate with an explicit error term.

outcomes.description: Calculate integer rings, ideal factorizations, norms, ramification and elementary class-group examples in number fields.
Use multiplicative functions, Euler products, summation by parts and elementary zeta or Dirichlet-series continuation to derive bounded prime and divisor estimates.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology Foundations
decks.description: Compute algebraic invariants of shape.

includes: Homotopy, fundamental groups, van Kampen and covering spaces.

practice: Compute invariants and coverings for glued spaces and prove a noncontractibility result.

outcomes.description: Prove path and homotopy lifting and relate connected coverings to subgroups under explicit local hypotheses.
Construct homotopies and compute fundamental groups of elementary spaces using deformation retractions and van Kampen.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Advanced Combinatorics
decks.description: Analyze families of finite structures.

includes: Generating functions, enumeration, extremal graphs, matching, coloring and probabilistic methods.

practice: Solve an enumeration problem in two representations and write a probabilistic existence proof.

outcomes.description: Construct ordinary and exponential generating functions and extract coefficients for recurrences, partitions and labeled structures.
Prove matching, coloring and extremal results and use expectation, alteration and random graphs for existence and threshold bounds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional Analysis
decks.description: Analyze infinite-dimensional operators and equations.

includes: Lp, Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality, bounded operators, compact spectra and variational problems.

practice: Develop an operator proof and a variational existence argument with explicit counterexamples to weakened assumptions.

outcomes.description: Prove core completeness, duality, uniform-boundedness, open-mapping and compact self-adjoint spectral results for specified function spaces.
Formulate coercive bilinear problems, prove existence and uniqueness through Hilbert-space representation and derive Galerkin error bounds.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Logic
decks.description: Analyze formal reasoning and its limits.

includes: First-order logic, completeness, arithmetic encoding, incompleteness and axiomatic sets.

practice: Develop a formal proof and countermodel pair and a delimited metatheorem with encoding assumptions.

outcomes.description: Encode syntax and prove a precisely stated incompleteness result, distinguishing truth, provability and decidability.
Construct formal derivations and models and prove soundness and first-order completeness through explicit model construction.
Reason about ordinals, cardinals and choice within elementary set axioms and distinguish dependence and relative consistency claims.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical PDEs
decks.description: Implement and validate spatial discretizations.

includes: Finite differences, finite volumes, boundary implementation and numerical PDE stability.

practice: Compare two spatial schemes on smooth and nonsmooth data and report boundary and stability failures.

outcomes.description: Implement finite-difference and finite-volume schemes for elliptic, diffusion and transport problems in one and two dimensions.
Derive consistency and von Neumann stability conditions and assess convergence using conservation, refinement and manufactured solutions.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Riemannian Geometry
decks.description: Derive metric geometry and curvature.

includes: Connections, geodesics, parallel transport, curvature and elementary global metric results.

practice: Analyze geodesics and curvature for contrasting metrics and distinguish coordinate from geometric singularities.

outcomes.description: Derive Levi-Civita connections, covariant derivatives and geodesic equations and calculate parallel transport in explicit metrics.
Calculate curvature tensors, sectional curvature and geodesic deviation and prove elementary metric completeness and comparison consequences under stated hypotheses.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Statistics
decks.description: Derive and validate statistical estimators.

includes: Likelihood, Bayesian inference, multivariate distributions, regression, diagnostics and decision theory.

practice: Implement an estimator, test interval coverage on generated data and analyze a multivariable dataset.

outcomes.description: Compare tests, intervals and losses, control multiple testing and distinguish predictive, causal and decision claims.
Derive likelihood and conjugate Bayesian estimators, sufficiency, bias, consistency and information bounds; calculate multivariate Gaussian conditioning.
Implement linear, logistic and Poisson regression using matrix and Newton formulations and diagnose residuals, collinearity and misspecification.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics
decks.description: Connect light-matter mechanisms to measurements.

includes: Atomic structure, field shifts, coherent driving, lasers, resonators and spectroscopy.

practice: Analyze an approved spectroscopy experiment and discriminate linewidth or level-shift mechanisms.

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary multielectron, fine, hyperfine and external-field shifts through angular coupling and perturbation.
Derive driven two-level dynamics and laser rate equations and explain resonators, linewidths and bounded cooling and trapping models.
Infer transitions, temperatures and interaction parameters from calibrated spectra, separating instrumental and physical broadening.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Classical Mechanics
decks.description: Derive analytical models of constrained motion.

includes: Spatial rigid-body dynamics, generalized coordinates, constrained variation, Hamiltonian mechanics and nonlinear stability.

practice: Derive a constrained spatial mechanism in Newtonian, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian representations.

outcomes.description: Solve central-force, rotating-frame and three-dimensional rigid-body problems using inertia tensors and angular momentum.
Analyze coupled modes, nonlinear phase portraits, resonance and elementary chaotic sensitivity and distinguish local and global stability.
Derive Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton equations, constrained motion, Poisson brackets and Noether conservation laws.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Graduate Electrodynamics
decks.description: Analyze advanced radiation and electromagnetic response.

includes: Covariant electrodynamics, retarded fields, radiation, dispersion, causality and Green-tensor methods.

practice: Derive a radiating-source observable and compare dispersive scattering predictions with causal and energy constraints.

outcomes.description: Derive causal dispersion relations and solve bounded dispersive-media scattering problems using Green functions, matching and asymptotic approximations.
Derive covariant field transformations and retarded potentials and calculate radiation from relativistic trajectories and multipole sources.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
decks.description: Infer subatomic structure through reactions and detection.

includes: Nuclear structure, decay, reactions, particles, symmetries, collision kinematics and detectors.

practice: Reconstruct decay or collision records and compare hypotheses including detector effects.

outcomes.description: Explain tracking, energy loss, calorimetry and counting and reconstruct bounded events with efficiency, background and uncertainty.
Calculate binding, decay chains, thresholds and liquid-drop or shell-model predictions and interpret nuclear scattering evidence.
Organize particles and interactions by symmetries and quantum numbers and calculate collision kinematics and elementary cross-section observables.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical-Mechanical Foundations
decks.description: Connect microscopic probability to thermal observables.

includes: State counting, classical ensembles, partition functions and fluctuations in ideal models.

practice: Derive a microscopic heat-capacity model and compare it with measured thermal data.

outcomes.description: Calculate ideal-gas, spin and oscillator energy, pressure, heat capacity, entropy and fluctuations and compare ensemble assumptions.
Construct microcanonical and canonical probabilities and partition functions from specified classical or discrete energy states.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell Biology
decks.description: Infer cellular organization and regulation.

includes: Organelles, membranes, cytoskeleton, trafficking, signaling, cell cycle and cellular disease mechanisms.

practice: Infer a trafficking or signaling mechanism from images and perturbations and design a rescue experiment.

outcomes.description: Explain cell-cycle control, differentiation, apoptosis and oncogenic disruption and compare mechanisms against time-course evidence.
Explain compartmentation, cytoskeletal organization and membrane trafficking and interpret localization, fractionation and live-cell imaging.
Construct signaling diagrams with feedback and infer pathway order using perturbation and rescue evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation Biology
decks.description: Translate ecological evidence into conservation action.

includes: Abundance, detection, viability, conservation genetics, restoration and management decisions.

practice: Produce a conservation assessment from imperfect survey data and defend an intervention against alternatives.

outcomes.description: Compare habitat, restoration, harvest and genetic-management options using ecological predictions, costs, community interests and uncertainty-sensitive criteria.
Estimate abundance and occupancy with taught mark-recapture and repeated-detection likelihoods using explicit grid maximization; calculate finite-stage viability projections and uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics
decks.description: Infer genomic structure and function computationally.

includes: Sequence processing, assembly, alignment, variants, expression analysis, reproducibility and governance.

practice: Analyze approved sequencing data from reads to a validated biological claim, including an implemented core algorithm.

outcomes.description: Build reproducible workflows with provenance and justify consent, ancestry-reference, reidentification and sharing decisions.
Infer variants and differential expression using taught sequencing-error and overdispersed count likelihoods and evaluate multiplicity, reference bias and biological alternatives.
Implement k-mer counting, dynamic-programming alignment and small graph assembly and run documented read-quality, mapping and annotation workflows.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology and Virology
decks.description: Investigate microbial mechanisms and consequences.

includes: Microbial cultivation, metabolic diversity, genetic exchange, viral replication and host interactions.

practice: Analyze a contained identification and growth study with contamination controls and mechanistic susceptibility interpretations.

outcomes.description: Plan approved low-risk culture, staining, enumeration and identification; calculate growth and dilution and diagnose contamination and cultivation bias.
Compare colonization, infection, resistance and transmission and evaluate susceptibility and prevention claims without clinical recommendations.
Explain bacterial and archaeal metabolism, microbial communities, horizontal transfer and viral replication from molecular evidence.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Physiology and Development
decks.description: Predict and measure plant function and growth.

includes: Plant transport, nutrition, photosynthesis, hormones, reproduction and environmental responses.

practice: Measure an environmental response and reconcile water balance, gas exchange and growth evidence.

outcomes.description: Design plant experiments accounting for acclimation, developmental stage, environmental gradients and destructive sampling.
Explain meristems, hormones, flowering, reproduction and stress responses in anatomical and life-cycle context.
Apply taught water-potential and mass-balance models to xylem, phloem, stomata and mineral uptake and interpret gas-exchange measurements.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology
decks.description: Recover macromolecular structure from indirect evidence.

includes: Structural forward models, diffraction, cryo-EM, NMR restraints, regularized reconstruction and validation.

practice: Reconstruct a toy density and audit a public structure against maps or restraints and held-out evidence.

outcomes.description: Construct discrete three-dimensional density, Fourier-scattering and projection models and interpret NMR distance restraints, phases, orientation and heterogeneity.
Derive and implement quadratic regularized least-squares reconstruction through normal equations and use documented crystallographic or cryo-EM refinement workflows.
Validate structures with held-out measurements, map agreement, stereochemistry and alternative conformations and bound functional claims by resolution.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Analysis and Chemometrics
decks.description: Develop validated advanced chemical measurements.

includes: Hyphenated instruments, tandem mass spectrometry, multidimensional NMR, sensors and chemometrics.

practice: Develop a raw-signal-to-composition workflow and challenge it with blinded mixtures and interferents.

outcomes.description: Design LC-MS/MS, two-dimensional NMR or coupled-sensor measurements and derive bounded separation, fragmentation, coherence and transduction response models.
Implement multivariate calibration and spectral unmixing using covariance eigenmodels, constrained least squares and explicitly derived latent-component regression.
Validate traceability, recovery, robustness and interlaboratory agreement and defend fitness-for-purpose and uncertainty claims.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Materials Chemistry
decks.description: Connect molecular statistics and defects to materials design.

includes: Polymer statistical mechanics, phase separation, solid defects, ion transport and advanced material design.

practice: Defend a polymer or energy-material design through quantitative structure-processing-property models and uncertainty.

outcomes.description: Derive ideal-chain dimensions, entropic elasticity and bounded polymer-mixing phase diagrams and infer architecture from scattering and rheological evidence.
Calculate defect equilibria and ionic transport and compare electronic-structure and interfacial explanations of functional-solid performance using complementary characterization.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Electronic Structure
decks.description: Implement and audit electronic-structure calculations.

includes: Self-consistent electronic calculations, basis convergence, correlation and density-functional comparisons.

practice: Implement a toy self-consistent calculation and audit a molecular prediction across basis and approximation choices.

outcomes.description: Implement restricted Hartree-Fock self-consistency from supplied integrals, including overlap orthogonalization, Fock construction, density updates and convergence diagnostics.
Use documented electronic-structure tools to compare basis, correlation and functional errors and validate energies, geometries and frequencies against independent evidence.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry and Geochemistry
decks.description: Predict environmental chemical fate and infer sources.

includes: Atmospheric, aquatic and geological chemistry, speciation, transport compartments, source inference and remediation.

practice: Investigate a watershed, atmospheric or soil case and defend source and remediation conclusions against alternatives.

outcomes.description: Calculate speciation, redox, sorption, partitioning and finite-time compartment mass balances using explicitly taught fate models.
Design environmental sampling and source-discrimination studies and compare remediation options with uncertainty, exposure and community consequences.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Surface and Colloid Chemistry
decks.description: Quantify interfacial chemical behavior.

includes: Adsorption, capillarity, electrochemical interfaces, colloids, surfactants and surface characterization.

practice: Fit competing adsorption and colloidal-stability models and design a discriminating surface measurement.

outcomes.description: Calculate micellization and colloidal stability in taught free-energy models and infer interface mechanisms from adsorption, scattering and electrochemical data.
Derive adsorption isotherms, surface-excess and curvature-pressure relations and bounded double-layer and interfacial electron-transfer models.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Molecular Simulation
decks.description: Implement molecular dynamics and equilibrium sampling.

includes: Classical force fields, molecular dynamics, periodic boundaries, Monte Carlo, free energy and correlated uncertainty.

practice: Simulate a molecular fluid and compare thermodynamic estimates across integration and sampling methods.

outcomes.description: Implement pair and bonded forces and velocity-Verlet integration with periodic boundaries; analyze ensembles, constraints, energy conservation and sampling adequacy.
Derive and implement Metropolis sampling and bounded free-energy reweighting or umbrella integration and estimate autocorrelation-aware uncertainty.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Photochemistry
decks.description: Explain and measure light-driven molecular change.

includes: Excited-state pathways, photophysical kinetics, photochemical reactions and time-resolved measurement.

practice: Analyze a quenching or photoreaction dataset with competing kinetic models and an uncertainty-aware follow-up design.

outcomes.description: Infer lifetimes and pathways from steady and time-resolved spectra using instrument-response convolution and explicit grid fitting; distinguish photophysics from net chemistry.
Construct excited-state diagrams and derive fluorescence, quenching and competing-reaction yields from rate equations, accounting for spin and selection rules.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Synthesis and Organometallic Chemistry
decks.description: Design and evaluate molecular construction.

includes: Retrosynthesis, selectivity, organometallic mechanisms, catalytic cycles and route evaluation.

practice: Defend competing multistep syntheses and execute an approved segment or analyze authentic laboratory records.

outcomes.description: Construct catalytic cycles with electron counting, oxidative addition, insertion and elimination and predict bounded ligand and substrate effects.
Develop retrosynthetic disconnections and forward routes using bond construction, redox, protection and stereoselective transformations.
Compare routes by yield, selectivity, impurity control, hazards and waste and specify characterization and contingency evidence.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Graduate Distributed Systems
decks.description: Build services under explicit failure models.

includes: Consensus, replication, consistency, impossibility, transactions and distributed service evaluation.

practice: Build a replicated store with model-based history checking and a safety and liveness argument.

outcomes.description: Specify safety and liveness and implement a crash-tolerant replicated consensus log with leader-change and state-machine checks.
Prove quorum and elementary asynchronous-consensus impossibility results, distinguishing synchrony, fairness and failure detection.
Design sharded transactional services and compare consistency, recovery and availability under fault-injected workloads.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning
decks.description: Derive and implement statistical learning machinery.

includes: Regularized prediction, latent models, Bayesian networks, neural networks and reinforcement learning.

practice: Implement baselines and a learned system with held-out evaluation, ablations, uncertainty and a deployment judgment.

outcomes.description: Implement clustering, principal components and finite-mixture EM and calculate inference in small Bayesian networks.
Derive and implement backpropagation and train feedforward and convolutional models with optimization and overfitting diagnostics.
Implement regularized regression, trees and kernels and evaluate calibration, subgroup error and leakage-free model selection.
Formulate finite Markov decision processes and implement value iteration and tabular Q-learning, assessing exploration and reward misspecification.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics and Control
decks.description: Integrate sensing, physical models and action.

includes: Rigid-body kinematics, feedback, state estimation, localization and collision-aware motion planning.

practice: Implement a simulated robot with noisy sensors, constrained planning and feedback and validate estimation consistency and fail-safe behavior.

outcomes.description: Construct rigid transforms and manipulator Jacobians and derive bounded dynamics, linear feedback and finite-horizon quadratic control with Riccati recursions.
Derive Kalman and extended-Kalman updates from Gaussian state and observation models and diagnose observability and inconsistent uncertainty.
Implement configuration-space collision checking and sampling-based planning and assess integrated estimation, control and safety under model errors.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Security and Privacy Engineering
decks.description: Assess and reduce risks in functioning systems.

includes: Threat modeling, cryptographic interfaces, vulnerability analysis, defenses and privacy judgment.

practice: Audit an intentionally vulnerable local application and deliver fixes, authorized tests and a risk decision.

outcomes.description: Demonstrate and remediate memory, injection, authentication, authorization and network flaws in isolated systems and validate negative cases.
Compare disclosure, surveillance, privacy and availability obligations and justify proportionate controls and residual risk.
Specify assets, adversaries and trust boundaries and correctly use encryption, hashes, signatures, authenticated transport and password-storage interfaces.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Advanced Logic
decks.description: Develop model-theoretic and computability continuations.

includes: Compactness, elementary models, types, quantifier elimination and relative computability.

practice: Prove a model-construction theorem and a hierarchy separation with explicitly represented syntax and oracles.

outcomes.description: Construct oracle computations and reductions, analyze the arithmetic hierarchy and prove bounded degree or undefinability results.
Prove compactness and Löwenheim-Skolem consequences and analyze elementary equivalence, types and quantifier elimination in a specified algebraic theory.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate PDE Analysis
decks.description: Prove existence and stability of weak PDE solutions.

includes: Distributions, Sobolev spaces, weak elliptic and evolution equations, estimates and regularity.

practice: Prove a complete weak-solution theorem and identify which estimates survive nonsmooth data.

outcomes.description: Construct weak heat and wave solutions using Galerkin approximation, derive a priori estimates and establish bounded regularity and uniqueness results.
Define distributions, weak derivatives and Sobolev spaces; prove energy estimates and existence for bounded-domain elliptic equations using coercivity and compactness.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Statistics
decks.description: Analyze advanced inference procedures and their limits.

includes: Asymptotic inference, estimating equations, hierarchical Bayesian computation and nonparametric estimation.

practice: Compare asymptotic, bootstrap and posterior uncertainty on regular and deliberately nonregular datasets.

outcomes.description: Derive delta-method and M-estimator limits and likelihood asymptotics and identify failures under nonregular or dependent sampling.
Implement hierarchical Bayesian models with derived Metropolis or Gibbs transitions and kernel nonparametric estimators; assess convergence, bandwidth, uncertainty and posterior predictive fit.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Global and Algebraic Topology
decks.description: Connect global invariants and differential forms.

includes: Chain complexes, homology, cohomology, manifold integration and de Rham theory.

practice: Compute global invariants of selected manifolds using both chains and differential forms.

outcomes.description: Construct partitions of unity, prove manifold Stokes results and calculate de Rham classes and their topological correspondence.
Construct chain complexes, calculate cellular homology and elementary cohomology products and use exact sequences.

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Stochastic Processes
decks.description: Analyze random evolution rigorously.

includes: Conditional expectation, martingales, continuous-time Markov processes, Brownian motion and Itô calculus.

practice: Prove a stopping claim and derive an SDE's moments and stationary law with explicit integrability conditions.

outcomes.description: Define conditional expectation and filtrations and prove selected martingale convergence and stopping results.
Construct Poisson and continuous-time Markov processes and Brownian motion and derive generators and transition equations.
Construct Itô integrals, apply Itô's formula and solve elementary SDEs, distinguishing strong, weak and deterministic interpretations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Advanced Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Use graduate quantum representations.

includes: Scattering, propagators, path integrals, Fock space, mixed states, channels and open dynamics.

practice: Calculate a scattering observable and open two-level evolution in complementary representations.

outcomes.description: Construct bosonic and fermionic Fock states and Hamiltonians and calculate many-particle matrix elements and correlations.
Use density operators, partial traces, entanglement and channels and derive bounded master-equation models of decoherence and measurement.
Derive propagator and scattering formulations, partial waves, Born approximations and elementary path integrals with unitarity checks.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astrophysics and Cosmology
decks.description: Model astronomical systems from remote evidence.

includes: Radiative transfer, stellar structure, planetary and galactic dynamics and homogeneous cosmology.

practice: Compare stellar, planetary or cosmological forward models with calibrated observations and selection-sensitive alternatives.

outcomes.description: Apply explicitly developed Friedmann and thermal-history models to redshift and distance and assess evidence for dark matter and dark energy.
Derive radiative-transfer and stellar-structure equations and connect spectra, hydrostatic balance, nuclear energy budgets and evolutionary stages.
Analyze planetary orbits, transit and velocity signals and galaxy rotation and distinguish selection from inferred mass and populations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Computational Physics
decks.description: Implement and validate computational physical models.

includes: Particle and field simulation, eigenproblems, Monte Carlo and physical validation.

practice: Deliver a reproducible simulation with invariant tracking, error studies and independent physical validation.

outcomes.description: Implement symplectic particle integration and finite-grid wave or Schrödinger evolution and compare conservation, stability and spectral errors.
Implement Metropolis sampling for a spin or particle model and estimate thermodynamic observables with blocking-based correlated uncertainty.
Design verification and validation using analytic limits, manufactured solutions, refinement, independent implementations and measurements.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed-Matter Physics
decks.description: Explain solid properties from microscopic structure.

includes: Lattices, diffraction, phonons, electronic bands, transport, semiconductors and collective phases.

practice: Infer lattice and electronic models from diffraction and transport data and test a phase-transition explanation.

outcomes.description: Derive Bloch, nearly-free and tight-binding models; develop Fermi occupation locally and calculate effective mass and elementary transport.
Construct reciprocal lattices and diffraction conditions and derive lattice-vibration dispersions and phonon heat capacities.
Compare magnetic and superconducting phases through explicitly developed exchange and mean-field pairing models and interpret structural, thermal and transport evidence.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Continuum Mechanics and Fluids
decks.description: Model deformable solids and fluids.

includes: Continuum balances, stress, elasticity, viscous flow, boundary layers and rotating geophysical flows.

practice: Simulate a two-dimensional flow or elastic wave and validate dimensionless regimes and convergence.

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balances and Cartesian stress-strain relations and solve elementary elastic deformation and waves.
Derive and nondimensionalize Navier-Stokes equations and analyze pipe flow, vorticity, boundary layers and rotating or stratified approximations.
Implement a bounded continuum discretization and assess constitutive assumptions, boundaries and resolution against analytic or measured benchmarks.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: General Relativity
decks.description: Derive gravitational dynamics in curved spacetime.

includes: Lorentzian geometry, Einstein equations, black holes, cosmology, geodesics and gravitational waves.

practice: Derive a metric's curvature and geodesic observables and analyze a bounded linear perturbation.

outcomes.description: Extend metric and connection calculations to Lorentzian signature and derive stress-energy, geodesic and Einstein equations from variational principles.
Linearize gravitational equations under stated gauges and derive wave propagation and leading detector consequences.
Analyze Schwarzschild and homogeneous cosmological solutions, horizons and orbital observables with coordinate-singularity checks.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Graduate Classical Dynamics
decks.description: Analyze advanced Hamiltonian and nonlinear behavior.

includes: Canonical transformations, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, action-angle methods, perturbation and nonlinear dynamics.

practice: Compare perturbative and numerical descriptions of a near-integrable system and document resonance and convergence limits.

outcomes.description: Construct canonical transformations, solve bounded Hamilton-Jacobi problems and derive action-angle and averaging approximations near integrable motion.
Analyze bifurcations, Poincaré maps and Lyapunov exponents; implement structure-preserving integration and distinguish numerical chaos from physical instability.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Plasma Physics
decks.description: Predict collective behavior of ionized matter.

includes: Charged-particle orbits, screening, plasma waves, fluid closures, MHD and kinetic distributions.

practice: Analyze a laboratory or space-plasma dataset and compare particle, fluid and kinetic explanations in their validity regimes.

outcomes.description: Derive two-fluid and ideal-MHD equations from balances and calculate elementary electrostatic, Alfvén and magnetosonic dispersion and stability.
Formulate phase-space Vlasov dynamics, derive moment closures and interpret resonant damping and diagnostic distributions without claiming a full kinetic stability proof.
Calculate gyromotion, guiding-center drifts, Debye screening and collisional scales and assess confinement approximations.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Graduate Statistical Mechanics
decks.description: Explain collective thermal behavior.

includes: Quantum ensembles, interacting systems, critical phenomena and near-equilibrium response.

practice: Compare exact, mean-field and coarse-grained predictions and derive a measurable transport response.

outcomes.description: Analyze Ising, transfer-matrix and mean-field models and derive elementary scaling and coarse-graining recursions.
Derive grand-canonical, Bose and Fermi distributions and calculate quantum-gas observables and ensemble equivalence limits.
Derive master-equation balance and bounded transport and fluctuation-dissipation relations with specified equilibrium assumptions.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Comparative Animal Physiology
decks.description: Explain integrated animal function quantitatively.

includes: Comparative organ systems, transport, electrophysiology, muscle and endocrine feedback.

practice: Interpret a multichannel physiological record using transport balances and feedback predictions.

outcomes.description: Calculate equilibrium potentials and conductance currents using taught ionic models and explain action potentials, synapses and contraction.
Analyze endocrine, reproductive and thermal feedback and predict integrated exercise, dehydration and environmental responses.
Develop and apply bounded pressure-flow, diffusion, filtration and mass-balance models for circulation, respiration, digestion and renal function.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biotechnology and Synthetic Biology
decks.description: Design and assess benign biological engineering.

includes: Contained genetic engineering, expression, screening, bioprocess balances and biotechnology governance.

practice: Design a contained benign biosensor or production workflow and assess performance and governance through approved evidence.

outcomes.description: Design benign recombinant expression or editing constructs and assembly and screening workflows with specificity, off-target and functional validation controls.
Evaluate containment, ecological uncertainty, intellectual property, access and dual-use implications and justify restrictions or alternatives.
Calculate batch-growth and product balances using taught yield and saturation models and compare expression, purification and scale-up constraints.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Infer construction of multicellular form.

includes: Lineage, fate specification, gradients, morphogenesis, organogenesis and regeneration.

practice: Reconstruct a developmental mechanism from lineage images and design a spatially and temporally controlled test.

outcomes.description: Explain cell movement, adhesion, tissue folding, organogenesis and regeneration and compare conserved and convergent developmental mechanisms.
Infer lineage, competence, induction and positional information from tracing and perturbations using explicitly taught gradient-threshold models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Graduate Eco-Evolutionary Modeling
decks.description: Infer ancestry and coupled population processes.

includes: Coalescent ancestry, demographic inference, ecological-evolutionary dynamics and hierarchical population models.

practice: Compare population histories and coupled dynamics through synthetic recovery and independent biological evidence.

outcomes.description: Derive and simulate finite-population and coalescent models and compare demographic, selective and migration histories using explicit sequence likelihoods.
Analyze ecological-evolutionary ODE and patch models through equilibria, invasion criteria, stability and numerical perturbations.
Fit hierarchical observation and population models and assess detection bias, identifiability and out-of-sample prediction.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immunity and evaluate intervention evidence.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunity, receptor diversity, regulation, immunopathology and assay interpretation.

practice: Analyze a blinded immune-assay panel and compare mechanism and intervention explanations.

outcomes.description: Interpret antibody, flow-cytometry and cellular-response assays with controls and justify benefit-risk conclusions from intervention evidence.
Explain memory, tolerance, inflammation, hypersensitivity, autoimmunity and tumor immunity through regulatory mechanisms.
Trace recognition, antigen presentation, lymphocyte activation and effector responses and explain receptor diversity and tissue organization.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Computational Molecular Biophysics
decks.description: Assess molecular simulations of biological function.

includes: Biomolecular force fields, conformational ensembles, binding free energy and structural validation.

practice: Audit a bounded biomolecular conformational or binding calculation against experimental observables.

outcomes.description: Construct protein or nucleic-acid simulation representations with solvent, protonation and parameter choices and compare conformational and binding models.
Validate sampled ensembles against structural or spectroscopic observables and separate force-field, sampling and observation-model uncertainty.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Regulation
decks.description: Evaluate molecular regulation at advanced experimental depth.

includes: Chromatin, transcription, RNA regulation, proteostasis and complementary advanced perturbation methods.

practice: Reconstruct a regulatory mechanism from conflicting records and defend a multi-assay causal test.

outcomes.description: Design complementary chromatin, proteomic, reporter and imaging studies and interpret processed data with specificity, timing and indirect-effect controls.
Compare chromatin, transcriptional, RNA-processing and protein-turnover mechanisms using explicit occupancy, interaction and feedback models.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology
decks.description: Construct and challenge quantitative biological mechanisms.

includes: Biochemical networks, ODE and master equations, stochastic simulation, identifiability and experimental design.

practice: Implement deterministic and stochastic regulatory models, fit imperfect data and design a separating perturbation.

outcomes.description: Estimate parameters from time series and analyze sensitivity, structural and practical identifiability and competing network explanations.
Construct stoichiometric ODE and master-equation models and implement Gillespie sampling from derived propensities and waiting-time distributions.
Design informative perturbations and evaluate held-out predictions, conservation laws and biological plausibility.

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Molecular Reactivity
decks.description: Discriminate molecular mechanisms quantitatively.

includes: Transition-state models, isotope and substituent effects, spin states, electron transfer and ligand dynamics.

practice: Develop a mechanism-discrimination dossier with conflicting evidence and a decisive proposed experiment.

outcomes.description: Analyze ligand-field and orbital descriptions, spin states, electron transfer and substitution and reconcile catalytic cycles with rates and thermodynamics.
Derive predictions from transition-state, substituent, isotope and stereoelectronic models and compare organic pathways using kinetic and spectral evidence.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Learning Theory and Advanced Models
decks.description: Analyze learning guarantees and advanced model behavior.

includes: Generalization theory, capacity, advanced representation and generative learning and research evaluation.

practice: Reproduce a bounded advanced-learning result and test its theoretical claims with controlled failures.

outcomes.description: Derive and implement bounded variational and autoregressive objectives and a discrete Gaussian diffusion chain, distinguishing inference, optimization and sampling errors.
Derive concentration, uniform-convergence and capacity bounds and analyze consistency and optimization assumptions and vacuous guarantees.
Design reproducible ablation, scaling and shift studies and justify robustness, privacy and societal claims with uncertainty.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Language Processing and Information Retrieval
decks.description: Construct retrieval and language-processing systems.

includes: Text representation, retrieval, sequence models, attention, language evaluation and linguistic error analysis.

practice: Build a retrieval and sequence-model pipeline and compare lexical and learned methods on documented linguistic error categories.

outcomes.description: Evaluate linguistic generalization, factuality and retrieval grounding using held-out and human-judged evidence and analyze multilingual, privacy and bias failures.
Implement n-gram and hidden-Markov models with smoothing and forward or Viterbi recurrences and derive attention-based sequence prediction objectives.
Implement tokenization, inverted indexes and lexical or vector ranking and evaluate relevance with precision, recall and rank-sensitive measures.

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Statistical Computer Vision
decks.description: Infer visual semantics with validated statistical models.

includes: Learned recognition, detection, segmentation and visual evaluation under shift.

practice: Train a visual model and challenge it with controlled shifts and annotated error analyses.

outcomes.description: Compare visual representations under viewpoint, illumination and domain shifts and assess localization error, subgroup performance and uncertainty.
Construct convolutional recognition, detection and segmentation objectives and implement training and spatial-output evaluation.

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory
decks.description: Compute relativistic quantum observables.

includes: Relativistic fields, quantization, propagators, scattering, regularization, renormalization and gauge foundations.

practice: Carry a simple interacting field theory from action to a renormalized observable with explicit conventions.

outcomes.description: Derive scalar, spinor and electromagnetic field equations and Noether currents and quantize free fields canonically and through path integrals.
Derive propagators and Feynman rules and calculate bounded tree and one-loop amplitudes with symmetry and dimensional checks.
Regularize and renormalize an elementary model and derive running couplings, explaining gauge constraints and effective-theory limits.

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience
decks.description: Connect neural mechanisms to behavior.

includes: Neural circuits, sensory and motor systems, plasticity, bounded coding models and causal experiments.

practice: Analyze neural and behavioral records and compare circuit models and discriminating interventions.

outcomes.description: Explain integration, sensory coding, motor control and learning through anatomically explicit circuit diagrams.
Interpret electrophysiology, imaging, lesion and stimulation evidence and distinguish correlation, representation and necessity while defending ethical choices.
Calculate an explicitly taught discrete-time integrate-and-fire model and population-rate code and distinguish states, observables and limitations.
